candidates.statement: A locally compact abelian group (LCA group) is a topological group L satisfying: 1. Abelian structure: xy = yx for all x, y ∈L. 2. Local compactness: Every point x ∈L admits a neighborhood whose closure is compact. 3. Hausdorff separation: Distinct points are separable via disjoint open sets. The combination of commutativity and local compactness ensures the existence of Haar measure and well-posed harmonic analysis.

candidates.statement: A homomorphism of LCA groups is a continuous group homomorphism between locally compact abelian groups. An isomorphism of LCA groups is a group isomorphism ϕ: L →H that is also a homeomorphism. In other words, it is a bijective continuous map whose inverse is also continuous.

candidates.statement: Let L be a locally compact abelian (LCA) group, equipped with its topology as a topological group. A Pontryagin character on L is a continuous group homomorphism χ: L →T, where T = {z ∈C | |z| = 1} is the circle group with its standard topology. The set of all such characters forms the Pontryagin dual group bL := Homcont(L, T), which is itself a topological group when endowed with the compact-open topology—that is, the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of L. This makes bL into an LCA group as well.

candidates.name: Balanced Edge
candidates.statement: Let X3,1 = {(T, e) | e is an edge of T} denote the set of edge–tetrahedron pairs in a triangulation X, and let ϕ : X3,1 →X1, (T, e) 7→e be the natural projection that assigns each local edge to its corresponding global edge in the triangulation. Given an angle structure θ : X3,1 →C := R × F ×, we say that an edge e ∈X1 is balanced if X (T,e)∈ϕ−1(e) θ(T, e) = (2, 1) ∈C. This condition expresses that the angle assigned around the edge e is 2π in the additive component and trivial in the multiplicative component. In other words, the sum of dihedral angles equals 2π, and the associated holonomy (interpreted multiplicatively) is trivial [1, 7].

The target space H1(∂M; C) parametrizes generalized boundary holonomies: that is, values of the angle structure assigned to edges lying in the boundary torus. These data specify the “external” parameters for the quantum wavefunction defined by the state-integral.

The condition H2(M; Z) = 0 is imposed for analytic reasons: it rules out closed normal surfaces that would cause squared Dirac δ-factors when the kine- matical kernel is multiplied by the pushed-forward dynamical content, see [1, Proof of Theorem 7] and [6]. candidates.statement: The balancing condition requires that the angle sum around each internal edge equals (2, 1) ∈C. This enforces a discrete flatness condition—zero holonomy around internal edges—which is essential for gluing consistency. It parallels the kernel constraints in Andersen–Kashaev [1], where vanishing holonomy ensures the state- integral is a well-defined distribution.

It also ensures that the product of the kinematical kernel and the dynam- ical content defines a well-behaved distribution after integrating out the internal edge parameters. More precisely, it guarantees that the quantum operator algebra defined by the edge equations is non-degenerate, which is necessary for consistent gluing. This mirrors the analytic condition in the TQFT construction of Andersen–Kashaev [1], where a gluing distribution GY is well-defined only when certain operator combi- nations vanish. These correspond to cycles generating ker[H1(∂M) →H1(M)], and their vanishing is equivalent to H2(M, Z) = 0.
